prize_parts.citation: For the development of targeted protein degradation, in which small molecules recruit E3 ubiquitin ligases to destroy chosen proteins, through PROTACs and the cereblon-dependent mechanism of thalidomide analogues

statement.case_for: I have moved my preferred configuration from molecular-sieve catalyst design (B044) to targeted protein degradation (B020). After round 1 my own ranking of B044 stands alone: no other member ranks it above the bottom of the list, and I said myself that field-closeness should discount my advocacy. B020 is the one candidate whose scientific case is accepted across members with very different backgrounds. Event-driven, catalytic removal of a protein through induced proximity is a new chemical and pharmacological principle, and it has been reproduced independently in many laboratories. The record also answers part of the maturity objection. The cereblon-dependent mechanism (Handa and Ito identified cereblon as the thalidomide target) explains the mode of action of approved drugs, so the strand with a proven clinical payoff sits next to the PROTAC concept (Crews and Deshaies, 2001) that supplies the design logic. A citation covering both mechanisms of recruiting an E3 ligase gives one coherent achievement in three names.
statement.case_against: No heterobifunctional degrader is approved, so the PROTAC half rests on mechanism and clinical-stage compounds, not on settled outcomes, and some colleagues will find the timing early. The three-name cap also forces real exclusions. Ciulli, whose structure-guided VHL work made degraders drug-like, is left out of my trio, as are Ito, Sakamoto, Kim and Gray, and any choice among them is partly a judgement about what the prize is for. A citation that joins PROTACs and glues may read as two discoveries joined for convenience. The molecular-sieve case I leave behind is also mature and has decades of industrial use; I am giving it up because of how the committee reads it (breadth, overlap with the 2025 framework prize), not because the science is weak.

responses.point: Proposes Crews, Deshaies and Handa for B020, with a citation widened to cover both PROTACs and the thalidomide-cereblon molecular-glue mechanism.
responses.response: I now agree with your structure. In round 1 I told Daniel Aili that a PROTAC-only prize would leave Handa and Ito unrecognised and that I would not accept that lightly, and I still hold that view. Handa's identification of cereblon is the mechanistic root of the only degrader drugs in patients, and it answers the maturity objection you raise yourself. I accept that a three-name limit means Ito and Ciulli are left out, and that is the price of a single coherent citation. I have therefore adopted your trio and nearly your wording.

responses.point: Argues for Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli, with Ciulli's structure-guided VHL design turning the concept into a design discipline, and treats Handa's cereblon work as target identification for an existing drug.
responses.response: Your point that the Ciulli work gives the field its design rules is strong, and it was my own opening choice for the third name. What changed my mind is that cereblon is more than target identification. Once Handa showed how thalidomide analogues recruit the ligase, the mechanism could be rationalised and exploited across the glue and PROTAC chemistries, and that is the part with approved drugs behind it. I think the committee is better served by a third name tied to demonstrated clinical outcome than by one tied to the design refinement of one ligase. I would put Ciulli first among the alternatives for the third place if the committee disagrees, and I accept that the exclusion needs to be discussed openly.

responses.point: Proposes a two-part prize pairing Cullis for ionizable lipid nanoparticles (B049) with Crews and Deshaies for the PROTAC concept.
responses.response: I see the logic of keeping the two achievements distinct, and the lipid chemistry is real chemistry. I do not follow you to a two-part prize, for two reasons. You yourself say that credit in B049 is unresolved and that Cullis alone understates a team effort that included industrial work. And a split leaves Crews and Deshaies without the cereblon mechanism, which I now think is needed to make B020 defensible. I would rather give B020 all three names and a single citation than weaken both parts.

responses.point: Pairs Pd-catalysed C-N coupling (B059) with covalent KRAS targeting (B058) and concedes that B059 may look like a second prize in an area covered in 2010.
responses.response: Attribution to Buchwald and Hartwig is clean, and I agree that four decades of use remove any maturity concern. Still, you concede the 2010 overlap, and I take that seriously for a related reason: I expect colleagues to read my own earlier candidate, molecular sieves, against the 2025 framework prize in the same way. A mature field that arouses a duplication worry is a harder sell than a new principle, even a younger one. Shokat's KRAS concept is singular and I take it seriously, but the cap then leaves two thin parts instead of one coherent one.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will accept a single citation that covers both PROTACs and cereblon-dependent glues, or sees them as two discoveries.
Whether Handa or Ciulli is the better third name, and how to weigh target identification and mechanism against structure-guided design.
Whether the absence of an approved PROTAC makes the timing too early, given that the approved drugs belong to the glue strand.
Whether Ito's exclusion, along with Sakamoto, Kim and Gray, can be defended under the three-person cap.
statement.conflict_note: My research field (electron crystallography of zeolites and other porous crystals) is close to B044, which was my round-1 first choice and is now an alternative; I flag this field-closeness again and no longer advocate that candidate as my lead. I have no known collaboration or institutional tie to the credited names on B044 or on B020. I am a Stockholm University colleague of Secretary Peter Brzezinski, which bears on none of the shortlisted candidates.
